I have been farming this same land for over forty years. I know Quzhou's soil — heavy loam, alkaline, needs plenty of water because the rains here are not reliable. My back is not what it was, and my son helps when he can, but mostly I manage myself and my daughter-in-law.

**Wheat (planted this October, harvested next June):**
I will plant all 14 mu to wheat after I rotary-till the maize stubble in. I always buy improved seed from the village supply station — I tried a new variety two years ago that my neighbor recommended, and it held up well against lodging. I apply base fertilizer when I plant: compound fertilizer plus extra nitrogen. Then I top-dress before jointing. I irrigate four times — before winter freeze, at jointing, heading, and grain filling. I spray herbicide early, then watch for aphids and powdery mildew in spring. That usually means three spray trips.

**Maize (planted this June right after wheat harvest):**
I will direct-seed maize without tilling — no time between harvest and planting, and my knees do not forgive me extra passes with the machine. I always use hybrid seed, everyone does now, the yields are much better than the old varieties my mother grew. I apply base fertilizer at planting and top-dress at jointing. Summer rains help but the well covers the gaps — I plan three irrigations. I spray herbicide once right after emergence and watch for corn borer in midsummer.

This is what I have always done. It feeds my family and leaves some grain to sell.
